title: The Maccabean Revolt
lead: The Jewish uprising of 167–160 BC against the Seleucid king Antiochus IV, who banned the Law and defiled the Temple. Led by the priest Mattathias and his son Judas Maccabeus, it ended with the Temple cleansed (remembered at Hanukkah) and later with an independent Jewish kingdom. Daniel 7–12, 1 Enoch 90 and 1–2 Maccabees all speak to it.

sections.h: The crisis and the books it produced
sections.b: In 167 BC Antiochus IV forbade circumcision, the Sabbath and the Temple sacrifices, and set up a pagan altar in the Temple, the "abomination that makes desolate" (1 Maccabees 1:41–64; Daniel 11:31). Mattathias and his sons took to the hills. Judas won a string of battles and cleansed the Temple in December 164 BC (1 Maccabees 4:36–59), the feast John 10:22 calls the Dedication. Most scholars date Daniel 7–12 and the Animal Apocalypse (1 Enoch 85–90) to these years: Daniel calls the fighters "a little help" (Daniel 11:34), while Enoch's vision gives Judas a great horn and the sheep a great sword (1 Enoch 90:9–19).
